central_question: For calendar year 2027: combined capex of the four major hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta) with a 70% confidence interval; whether global datacenter electricity consumption grows more than 20% year-over-year; and the probability that grid interconnection constraints delay more than 5 GW of planned US datacenter capacity into 2028.

situation_brief.current_situation: Combined 2026 capex guidance for the four hyperscalers stands at $720-745 billion, up ~77% from a 2025 record of roughly $410 billion; none has issued formal 2027 guidance as of 20 October 2026, but analyst consensus puts 2027 at $934.5 billion, with bank models at or above $1 trillion. Global datacenter electricity was 485 TWh in 2025 (+17%); the IEA central path implies ~14%/yr to ~950 TWh by 2030.
situation_brief.context: The AI buildout is funded by an accelerating shift from cash flow to debt (Meta $30B SPV, Oracle $18B, Alphabet $25B bond against >$115B book; lease commitments >$850B). Physical supply is the binding constraint: GE Vernova gas contracts at 116 GW targeting 125 GW by end-2026, new heavy-duty turbine lead times ~3 years, GSU transformer lead times >160 weeks, US interconnection queues >2,060 GW with median request-to-operation over five years, and 36.3 GW of US datacenter additions scheduled for 2027 against 8.5 GW energized in 2025.
situation_brief.dynamics: Analyst consensus has persistently lagged outcomes (2026 forecasts rose from ~$284B to >$525B); guidance moves in contagion after Alphabet's July 2026 raise. Grid friction is rising: PJM cut its summer-2027 peak ~4 GW on stricter datacenter vetting, Texas's ERCOT pause could delay 49.8 GW, and PJM's IRAS bring-your-own-capacity rules start June 2027. Only ~50-60% of scheduled capacity arrives on time.
